raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With speculative decoding, the default CUDA graph sizes now include every decode batch of 1 to 8 requests. Small
batches stop padding to the next power of two, which runs 1 + K extra tokens per padded request through every
layer.

## Claims

- With MTP K=3, 3, 5 and 7 running requests replay 12-, 20- and 28-token graphs instead of 16, 24 and 32. GLM-5.2-
  NVFP4, TP4, B300: decode -6% to -7% at 3 requests, -2.5% to -3.4% at 5, -2.2% to -2.4% at 7, unchanged at 1.
- Cost: three extra decode graphs (and their piecewise twins) for K=3: capture 6 s -> 7 s, graph memory +0.04 GiB
  per GPU (about 2,000 fewer KV cache tokens for GLM-5.3, 0.2%).
- Without speculation, and for explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes`, nothing changes.
- On InferenceX AgentX (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 4x GB200), decode time per turn drops 0.54% at concurrency 16 (4 runs each,
  95% CI [-0.93, -0.16]), where 37% of decode steps have 3 or more requests. At concurrency 1, 4 and 8 such steps
  are 0%, 4% and 13%, and the change is within run-to-run noise. No regression at any concurrency.

## Validation

- `tests/compile/test_config.py -k keep_all_sizes_bounded` (expected request grid updated) and
  `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py` pass. On B300, `tests/compile/test_config.py -k cudagraph` has the
  same 12 failures as main on that machine (`unchanged_without_speculation`, `respects_platform_ceiling`,
  `still_clamped_by_token_budget`, `test_use_cudagraphs`).
- Serving decode, B300 x4 (SM103), GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP K=3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step
  count), FP8 KV, default CUDA graph sizes, on top of the other GLM-5 decode changes. ms per token per request,
  median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts, before -> after:

  | context | 1 request | 3 requests | 5 requests | 7 requests |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 3.094 -> 3.097 | 4.300 -> 3.991 (-7.2%) | 5.134 -> 5.007 (-2.5%) | 5.662 -> 5.540 (-2.2%) |
  | 94K | 3.131 -> 3.119 | 4.370 -> 4.097 (-6.2%) | 5.265 -> 5.087 (-3.4%) | 5.788 -> 5.647 (-2.4%) |

- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, this PR on top of #62170, #62171, #62172 and #62174 (median
  per-turn change on the same turns, 95% CI; setup below). At concurrency 1 both runs capture the same graphs, so
  that column is a second reading of the noise:

  | concurrency | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | decode time | +0.5% [+0.4, +0.7] | -0.3% [-0.5, -0.1] | -0.1% [-0.4, +0.3] | -0.9% [-2.0, +0.2] |
  | e2e latency | +0.9% [+0.8, +1.1] | -0.3% [-0.5, -0.1] | -0.7% [-1.2, -0.4] | -1.1% [-2.0, -0.3] |
  | KV cache tokens | 0 | -0.2% | -0.2% | -0.2% |
  | main vs main, decode | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

- Three more c=16 runs each with and without this PR, interleaved (4 runs each; each run's median per-turn level
  against the per-turn median of all 8 runs): decode time -0.54% [-0.93, -0.16] (Welch), and every run with this
  PR is faster than every run without it (permutation p = 2/70). E2e latency -0.29% [-1.41, +0.82].

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and results for all GLM-5.3 PRs (4x GB200)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
with synthetic acceptance 2.99, native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, `max-num-seqs` = 2 x
concurrency. vLLM main dcd07967ca with its default backends and CUDA graph config, plus the PRs cumulatively in
the order below (FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631 and
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632 from #62174 on). One FlashInfer MoE autotune per concurrency, shared by all
variants. A fresh server per point, with the page cache dropped before each, and main run again at the end of
each concurrency as an A/A check. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM
all-reduce fusion and `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`.

Each cell is the median, over the turns both runs finished (150 to 520), of the per-turn ratio to the previous
variant, with a 95% paired bootstrap CI. Decode is request latency minus TTFT. The bootstrap does not include
run-to-run variance; the main-vs-main row does.

| decode time per turn | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| + #62170, #62171, #62172 | -2.8% [-3.1, -2.6] | -2.5% [-3.1, -1.7] | -1.5% [-2.2, -1.1] | -1.5% [-2.4, +0.3] |
| + #62174 | -1.6% [-1.8, -1.5] | -1.8% [-2.5, -0.9] | -3.3% [-3.9, -2.9] | -2.1% [-3.8, -0.9] |
| + #62173 | +0.5% (no-op here) | -0.3% [-0.5, -0.1] | -0.1% [-0.4, +0.3] | -0.9% [-2.0, +0.2] |
| all PRs vs main | -3.7% [-3.9, -3.5] | -4.3% [-4.8, -4.0] | -5.3% [-6.4, -4.8] | -4.8% [-6.5, -3.8] |
| main vs main (noise) | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

| e2e latency per turn | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| + #62170, #62171, #62172 | -3.3% | -1.8% | -1.2% | -0.6% |
| + #62174 | -1.4% | -1.4% | -2.7% | -1.6% |
| + #62173 | +0.9% | -0.3% | -0.7% | -1.1% |
| all PRs vs main | -4.1% | -3.4% | -4.7% | -3.8% |
| main vs main (noise) | -0.6% | -1.2% | +0.4% | -0.4% |

KV cache tokens per GPU (c=1 / 4 / 8 / 16): main 1,176,832 / 1,162,880 / 1,143,872 / 1,105,984; with all PRs
1,178,496 / 1,168,512 / 1,157,824 / 1,103,936. Window throughput (tok/s/GPU) moves up to 2.4% between runs in fast
mode, since it counts whichever long-context turns finish inside the 20 minutes; with all PRs it is +3.0%, -1.4%,
+4.8% and +1.2% at c=1/4/8/16.

vLLM vs SGLang, decode time per turn on the same turns (positive = vLLM slower):

| | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | +10.4% | +12.7% | +13.7% | -2.9% |
| all PRs | +6.2% | +7.5% | +5.7% | -6.9% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured as one group. `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3. #62173 changes only decode steps of 3, 5 or 7 requests; steps with 3 or
more requests are 0%, 4%, 13% and 37% of all steps at c=1/4/8/16. At c=1 both runs capture the same graphs, so
its +0.5% there is noise. At c=16, three more runs each of + #62174 and + #62173 (4 runs each, compared as
runs): decode time -0.54% [-0.93, -0.16], with every + #62173 run faster than every + #62174 run (permutation
p = 2/70); e2e latency -0.29% [-1.41, +0.82].

</details>

## Details

For speculative decoding, `_set_cudagraph_sizes` appends a request-count grid times `decode_query_len` (1 + K).
That grid started 1, 2, 4, 8, copied from the one-token grid, where padding 3 requests to 4 costs one token. A
decode request is 1 + K tokens, so the same padding costs 1 + K tokens. Padded tokens still go through the
attention, the GEMMs and the MoE (routed like real tokens), and at small batches decode is bound by those layers.
The token grid's 8-token stride already yields even request counts at K=3, so this adds 3, 5 and 7 requests there.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -692,7 +692,7 @@ def test_default_cudagraph_capture_sizes_keep_all_sizes_bounded():
     token_grid += list(range(256, token_grid_max + 1, 16))
 
     max_request_count = min(max_num_seqs, default_max_graph_size)
-    request_counts = [count for count in [1, 2, 4] if count <= max_request_count]
+    request_counts = list(range(1, min(max_request_count, 8) + 1))
     request_counts += list(range(8, min(max_request_count + 1, 256), 8))
     request_counts += list(range(256, max_request_count + 1, 16))
     request_counts.append(max_request_count)

@@ -2380,9 +2380,10 @@ def _set_cudagraph_sizes(self):
 
         `max_num_batched_tokens` is also appended to the list if it fits
         within `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, so the max batch size is captured
-        even when off-stride. Uniform decode sizes are appended when they fit
-        within the platform's default capture ceiling, since they need not land
-        on an 8- or 16-token stride.
+        even when off-stride. Uniform decode sizes (every request count up to
+        8, then 8- and 16-request strides, times the decode query length) are
+        appended when they fit within the platform's default capture ceiling,
+        since they need not land on an 8- or 16-token stride.
 
         In the end, `vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes`
         will be the final sizes to capture cudagraph (in ascending order).
@@ -2456,7 +2457,9 @@ def request_counts(max_reqs: int) -> list[int]:
                         # At most the platform default number of requests,
                         # mirroring the one-token-per-request decode ceiling.
                         max_reqs = min(max_reqs, default_max_graph_size)
-                        counts = [n for n in (1, 2, 4) if n <= max_reqs]
+                        # Every count up to 8: a padded request costs
+                        # decode_query_len tokens in every GEMM and MoE.
+                        counts = list(range(1, min(max_reqs, 8) + 1))
                         counts += list(range(8, min(max_reqs + 1, 256), 8))
                         counts += list(range(256, max_reqs + 1, 16))
                         return sorted(set(counts + [max_reqs]))
